open_points.subject: revocation visibility for an in-flight authenticated request
open_points.text: “Immediate” revocation is defined as “every request authenticated after the revocation commits observes it,” but A11’s formal invariant says a revoked grant, credential, viewer, or session “blocks the next authorization check immediately.”
open_points.question: If a request passes authentication before revocation commits but performs its project-scope or capability check afterward, must that request observe the revocation?
options: Only requests whose authentication completes after the revocation commit must observe it; an already-authenticated request may continue with cached identity or scope.
Every authorization check performed after the revocation commit must re-read the relevant persisted state and reject, even when the request authenticated earlier.
open_points.default_guess: Every post-commit authorization check observes the revocation and rejects the request.

witness.initial: An operator has an active staff session and an active assignment to project P.
events: The operator starts a request to read P; authorization_guard validates the session, then the request pauses before checking the assignment.
An administrator revokes the operator’s assignment to P and the revocation commits.
The operator’s request resumes and performs its project-scope authorization check.
outcomes: Under the request-authentication wording, the request authenticated before the commit and may complete the read.
Under the next-authorization-check invariant, the scope check observes the revoked assignment and rejects the read.
witness.observer: The operator sees project data in one implementation and an authorization rejection in the other.
